pr_title: Backfill: print created blocks only, add human-readable option
pr_body:
Fixes #8227 

cc @aSquare14 @beorn7 

Signed-off-by: Julien Pivotto <roidelapluie@inuits.eu>

pr_comments:
> Since creating multiple large blocks can take some time (we iterate over the entire file for every block), I think printing it right after creation would be nice to show the on-going progress instead of all at the end.

I will see how that is possible without printing the header each time.
@beorn7 do you want to take this for another ride?

Will have a look.

@aSquare14, could you, too? You are the domain expert for this code now. :-)

Alignment is just "nice to have", we should definitely not sacrifice printing all the details.

As suggested above, I think we can recycle the tabwriter, but we don't need to do it in this PR. I can try it out myself, and if it works, I'll create a follow-up PR.
Merged it to work on my follow-up PR.

issue_context.title: promtool tsdb backfill does not print newly created blocks
issue_context.body:
Given the following file:

```
foo 1 1
```

Running against an existing data dir:

```
./promtool tsdb create-blocks-from openmetrics test data
BLOCK ULID                  MIN TIME                       MAX TIME                       DURATION  NUM SAMPLES  NUM CHUNKS  NUM SERIES  SIZE
01ER00K5VBG2GB247EWJ7175GN  2020-11-24 18:00:00 +0000 UTC  2020-11-24 20:00:00 +0000 UTC  2h0m0s    35202        302         11          66KiB988B
```

And against a new data dir:

```
./promtool tsdb create-blocks-from openmetrics test datanew
BLOCK ULID                  MIN TIME                       MAX TIME                       DURATION  NUM SAMPLES  NUM CHUNKS  NUM SERIES  SIZE
01ER31PR9TNPXCGCEYFSAZR6VS  1970-01-01 00:00:01 +0000 UTC  1970-01-01 00:00:01 +0000 UTC  1ms       1            1           1           488B
```

I think that instead of printing the last block, we should print the newly-created blocks.

review_comments:
Minor issue here: The tabs are only aligned for the first block we print, because subsequent blocks are written with a new tabwriter.

Perhaps we can return the tabwriter and have it as an optional last argument in `printBlocks` (i.e. can be `nil`) so that we can recycle the first tabwriter?

Or something like that.
I need to check, but it only prints upon flush.
Which defeats the purpose of a live tail of created blocks
Flushing multiple times works but does not preserve alignment.
So let's accept that they will not be aligned, or maybe do not print the full line but only the ULID?

I think tabs not being aligned is okay but we should print the full line as the developer might want to check if the blocks are created correctly for which, mint, maxt, duration time would be helpful to see.
